**My reading: borderline, with the doubt on part 2. The page also makes this coverage only.**

**The page:** The quote is there word for word. The page is a Fast Company article by Harry McCracken, published 2026-05-22. He interviewed Hassabis during Google I/O week ("when I caught up with Hassabis this week"). It is a news report that quotes his own interview. It is not a transcript or a printed question-and-answer, so at best this is "pass, coverage only". The text around the quote, as it appears:

> Spark is rolling out first to users who subscribe to Google's high-end $100/month AI Ultra plan. Bringing it to the masses will involve its "adapting to the average person, adapting their workflows to this type of agentic assistance," says Hassabis. "It's probably going to play out over the rest of the year, would be my guess."

The page gives no exact day the words were said. It only places them in the week before 2026-05-22.

**The four parts:**
1. **Role:** Hassabis was chief executive of Google DeepMind in May 2026, which qualifies. **Pass.**
2. **Looks forward and is about AI:** **Borderline.** What "plays out" is the process of bringing Spark to everyone. The quoted words describe people adapting their work to agents ("adapting their workflows") more than anything the AI will do or a stated scale it will ship to. The link between "it" and "bringing it to the masses" is the reporter's own wording, not Hassabis's, and there is no number or test in it. You could read it as a forecast about deployment, but it is weak, and the rule says a truly borderline case stays out and is logged.
3. **Date:** "Over the rest of the year" has its own end, 31 December 2026. **Pass.** "Probably" and "would be my guess" are hedges, not probabilities.
4. **Source:** coverage only. Only the article's own quotes are available.

**Two things for the person checking:**
- **Possible overlap:** `2026-01-hassabis-agents-delegated-tasks-end-of-2026.toml` is close in gist (agents for ordinary people by the end of 2026). I don't treat this as the same claim, because the date, occasion and subject (the Spark rollout) differ. Please compare the two.
